transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-29
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Riley Chen (Redwood Product), Alex Moreno (LumenBridge CTO), Priya Singh (Head of Search), Dan Cole (SRE), Jamie Park (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Intro + qualification (10m): current stack uses Elastic + Pinecone for vectors, latency pain on long tail queries.
- Demo (30m): Hosted embeddings endpoint flow, rerank endpoint, Console insights, Optimize recommendations (batching + quantization suggestions).
- Security chat (8m): SOC2 question, SSO/SAML, data residency, retention.
- Next steps: pilot pricing, sample data ingest, hands-on studio.

Topics covered: hosted embeddings, reranker, API examples, Console tracing, Optimize suggestions, KV cache mention, batching tradeoffs, quantization, pilot scope, timeline, data residency, SOC2.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today, happy holidays by the way, we'll keep this to about 45-55 minutes. quick intro round?
[00:06] Alex (LumenBridge CTO): Hi, Alex here, CTO at LumenBridge. we're trying to improve search relevance across product pages and docs.
[00:11] Priya (Head of Search): Priya, I own search. right now we have Elastic for indexing and Pinecone for vector store, and we do a two-stage rerank.
[00:18] Samira: perfect, that gives us context. dan, jamie?
[00:20] Dan (SRE): Dan, SRE. i'm here for ops questions—VPC, egress, encryption.
[00:23] Jamie (Data Scientist): Jamie, i'll share sample queries and evaluation metrics.
[00:26] Miguel (Redwood SE): quick note — today we'll demo the hosted API path: embeddings endpoint, then the reranker API, show the Console metrics and Optimize suggestions. we'll also touch on cost/latency tradeoffs. sound good?
[00:32] Priya: yep, excited. last time we saw a demo there were some missing docs around reranker paramization.
[00:36] Miguel: cool, i'll show the default params and how you can tune scoring weights.
[00:39] Riley (Product): i'll call out new Optimize suggestions that recommend batch sizes and quant profiles based on your query distribution.
[00:44] Samira: all right, Miguel, take it away.

--- Demo start ---
[02:05] Miguel: i'll paste a quick cURL to hit the /embeddings endpoint. so typical flow: POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-1536, payload text list, returns embeddings. then you index into your vector DB (Pinecone, FAISS, etc).
[02:20] Miguel: note, our hosted embeddings are 1536 dims by default for that model, but you can pick other model sizes.
[02:28] Jamie: do you distort the vectors with any normalization server-side?
[02:31] Miguel: good Q—no surprise transforms, we return raw float32 vectors, you can request L2 or cosine in the rerank step. sometimes the transcript shows as "raw floats" or "row floats" in auto text but it's raw floats.
[03:00] Priya: latency—what are we seeing? our current tail is 350ms for vector lookup + rerank.
[03:05] Miguel: hosted embeddings call is typically 30-60ms p95 per text item for small batches, reranker call depends on sequence length—our reranker (re-rank endpoint) does a lightweight cross-encoder over top-K candidates. you can tune top_k. p95 for a single rerank on 8 candidates is often 90-180ms on hosted.
[03:20] Dan: and how does batching impact that? we often send 200 docs in a bulk job.
[03:25] Miguel: batching is great for throughput but increases latency for individual requests. Optimize will suggest continuous batching thresholds based on your qps and latency SLOs.
[04:12] Samira: show them the Console now — tracing and per-route cost.
[04:15] Riley: (screen share described) so here is the Console trace: you can see token-level breakdown, model time, and the caching hit rate. we have a prefix/KV cache but it shows up as "K V cash" sometimes in ASR which is cute but it's KV cache.
[04:36] Alex: interesting, so we can see which queries are cacheable?
[04:39] Riley: yeah, Console surfaces repetitive prefixes and suggests TTLs for cache entries.

[05:12] Miguel: now the rerank API—two options: 1) you can do a rerank-only endpoint that takes candidate vectors + query text and returns scored list, or 2) call the combined search endpoint which does vector lookup + rerank.
[05:28] Jamie: what's the input schema look like?
[05:31] Miguel: JSON: query, candidates (id + vector or id + doc text), model param, scoring metric. we'll paste the example.
[06:00] Priya: in the candidate list can we include metadata signals? click-through or recency?
[06:04] Miguel: yes — metadata fields are supported and can be weighted in the scoring function. that's a common ask.
[06:18] Dan: from an ops perspective—what about data retention on hosted? we don't want vectors stored long-term.
[06:23] Samira: hosted policy: short-term caching for performance, ingestion logs retained per plan, we have options for ephemeral-only retention and you can choose Private deployment if you need no-hosted retention.
[06:34] Alex: SOC2? and SAML?
[06:36] Samira: yes SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. we'll send SOC2 attestation and our security pack.

[07:10] Miguel: demonstration of rerank scoring — i'll show a few examples where we boost recency and demote duplicates.
[07:20] Miguel: here's a messy case where two docs are almost identical: reranker helps push the more authoritative doc up.
[07:34] Jamie: can we run offline evaluations? we'd like an easy way to compute MRR/NDCG across our query set.
[07:40] Riley: Optimize has an evaluation harness that runs your queries against candidate pools and reports MRR, NDCG, precision@k. Miguel will share the notebook.

[09:02] Miguel: performance note — if you send vectors to our rerank endpoint directly (avoiding double-deserialize), you can save ~15-25ms. it's a small trick.
[09:20] Priya: error modes—what happens if the reranker model is unavailable? fallback?
[09:23] Miguel: we have automated fallback policies: degrade to a cheaper model variant or return vector-similarity-only results. fallback policy is configurable per-route.

[11:45] Dan: if we move to Dedicated later, will the APIs change? we want minimal code churn.
[11:50] Samira: same API surface across hosted/dedicated/private, just different endpoints/credentials. the SDKs abstract that.
[12:05] Alex: are there quotas or rate limits we should know about for hosted?
[12:09] Samira: yes tiered quotas; for pilots we give elevated sandbox limits. we'll include those in the pilot doc.

[13:50] Miguel: now i want to show a quick tuning path: step 1 embed generation, step 2 vector store nearest neighbor recall, step 3 rerank with metadata features, step 4 evaluate and iterate. i'll walk through a notebook.
[14:12] Miguel: example — we had a retailer improve MRR by 12% by adding a recency feature and moving to a cross-encoder rerank on top 10.
[14:28] Jamie: do you support sparse + dense hybrid retrieval? hashed sparse signals?
[14:31] Miguel: yes hybrid retrieval is supported; you can combine Elastic sparse scores with vector scores client-side or using our combined endpoint.

[16:01] Riley: Optimize suggestions — here's a suggested batch window of 50ms to trade cost vs latency, and a quant profile if you choose a quantized private deployment.
[16:22] Alex: quantization on hosted — is that possible?
[16:24] Miguel: hosted has quantized model variants for lower-cost tiers; we also recommend dedicated if you need aggressive int8 quantization for latency. hosted quant is often q4h-like, but callouts vary by model.

[18:10] Priya: model drift concerns — if we retrain indices how do we track regressions?
[18:14] Riley: Console has eval baselines and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. you can pin model versions and get alerts on quality drops.

[20:00] Miguel: ok i'm going to run a live example: query "folding stroller compatibility" and show search candidates + rerank scores.
[20:04] (typing noises)
[20:22] Miguel: so top candidate before rerank was product A, after rerank product B (higher documentation match) — score moved from 0.62 to 0.81.
[20:35] Jamie: this matches our expectation for long-tail queries.

[23:00] Dan: network—we need VPC peering for private deployment. what about hosted egress?
[23:05] Samira: hosted is public but we support VPC peering on Redwood Private and Dedicated. for hosted we can restrict access via IP allowlist and use customer-managed keys for some plans.
[24:00] Alex: data residency — EU vs US?
[24:03] Samira: we have region controls, EU-only storage options; if you need strict residency we'll discuss Private.

[26:40] Priya: cost example—show me a sample unit cost for embeddings + rerank per 1M queries.
[26:45] Samira: rough example: embeddings cost X per 1k, rerank cross-encoder cost Y per call — i'll follow up with an exact pilot pricing sheet.
[27:10] Miguel: and the Console will show token-level spend so you can drill down per-query cost.

[30:15] Jamie: curious about annotation workflow integration — can we send human labels back to Optimize?
[30:18] Riley: yes Optimize has an import for labelled sets and will recompute evaluation metrics and suggest hyperparams.

[32:00] Alex: any customer references doing exactly this flow?
[32:03] Samira: yes, small retailer and a docs company — we'll share short case studies.

[33:45] Miguel: small gotcha to watch: vector dimensionality mismatch between your stored vectors and the model can cause silent failures. always version the model id in metadata.
[34:00] Jamie: good call. we'll include dims in our pipeline metadata.

[36:00] Priya: security follow-ups — can we get a security workshop with your security team?
[36:05] Samira: yes, we can schedule a security deep dive — Miguel will coordinate.

[38:00] Miguel: quick note on offline rerank: if you want to batch rerank many candidates for nightly scoring we have a batch rerank job API which is cost optimized.
[38:12] Dan: permisssion model for job API? admin-only?
[38:15] Riley: RBAC controls apply, we can scope keys to job-only.

[40:00] Samira: any other pressing questions?
[40:06] Alex: timeline — if we like the pilot, how fast can we get started?
[40:09] Samira: typical pilot starts within 1-2 weeks after SOW sign and data access. for this quarter we can try to start Jan week 2.

[42:00] Miguel: one more demo note — console query inspector shows per-candidate features used in rerank; it's useful to debug weird boosts.
[42:10] Jamie: can we export those features?
[42:13] Miguel: yes CSV export available.

[44:30] Riley: recap: 1) hosted embeddings + rerank supports your two-stage flow, 2) Console + Optimize give you evals and tuning suggestions, 3) security & residency options exist and Private/Dedicated if host policies don't match.
[44:50] Samira: next steps (recap): Samira will send pilot pricing + SOW, Miguel will share notebook and tuning checklist, Jamie will share 1k sample docs and query set.
[45:05] Alex: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[45:10] Priya: thanks, appreciate the detail.
[45:12] Dan: thanks.
[45:15] Samira: we'll send the recording and notes. happy holidays.

--- End transcript ---
